title: Why Your Shrink Should Prescribe Exercise - Nautilus
gist: A viewpoint paper by psychiatric researchers in Genomic Press argues clinicians should formally prescribe exercise for mental health rather than merely recommend it, grounding the case in a muscle-brain axis where contracting muscles release myokines that act on the brain.

insights.claim: A team of psychiatric researchers argues that medical professionals should prescribe exercise as a treatment rather than merely recommend it as lifestyle advice, given growing evidence it benefits the brain.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: A shift to prescribed exercise could expand reimbursable exercise-as-medicine services and digital fitness therapeutics in mental health.
insights.quote: Instead of merely recommending exercise as lifestyle advice, the team says they should prescribe it.
insights.locator: Exercise is good for your body

insights.claim: The viewpoint paper published in Genomic Press bases its argument on randomized trials, meta-analyses, and cohort studies.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Evidence base breadth matters for whether payers and guideline bodies adopt exercise prescriptions.
insights.locator: According to the team’s new viewpoint paper

insights.claim: The neurological benefits of exercise are attributed to a muscle-brain axis: contracting muscles release myokines, signaling proteins that act like hormones.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Myokine biology is a potential target for drugs mimicking exercise effects on cognition and mood.
insights.quote: When we contract our muscles, they release myokines (signaling proteins that act like hormones).
insights.locator: According to the team’s new viewpoint paper

insights.claim: Myokines are said to influence the brain through metabolic, inflammatory, neuroendocrine, and neurotrophic pathways, affecting both cognition and psychological state.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Multiple pathways suggest broad applicability across cognitive decline and mood disorders, relevant to neuro/psych therapeutics markets.
insights.quote: metabolic, inflammatory, neuroendocrine, and neurotrophic pathways
insights.locator: According to the team’s new viewpoint paper
